The framework is designed to scale dynamically—new languages, new metrics, and new models can be added as the field evolves. For entrepreneurs, this means trustworthy model comparison for any TTS-based product—from AI podcast generators to real-time translation tools to personalized audiobooks.

articles.hook: AI agents just got way smarter about knowing where info actually comes from.
articles.headline: MCP Agents Now Verify Facts by Checking the Source, Not Just the Claim
articles.body: HuggingFace has released a new approach to fact-checking for AI agents using Model Context Protocol (MCP) that fundamentally changes how verification works. Instead of just asking whether a statement is true or false, source-aware verification forces agents to trace back to where information originated and evaluate the credibility of that source. This matters because two agents can both say something is 'true' — but one checked a peer-reviewed study while the other checked a random blog post. The new framework enables MCP agents to distinguish between these scenarios, making them more reliable for high-stakes applications like legal research, medical information retrieval, or financial analysis. The system works by having agents maintain explicit awareness of their information chain: where did this fact come from, who published it, what's their track record, and does the source actually support what I'm claiming? This is especially valuable for enterprises building AI systems that need to be auditable and defensible — you can now trace exactly why an agent believed something and point to the source it used. Early implementations show this reduces hallucinations and false confidence significantly, though it does add latency since agents must verify sources rather than just pattern-match answers.
examples: Agent retrieves a claim about a drug interaction, traces it back to FDA database vs. Reddit, flags the difference.
Legal research bot cites case law with explicit source attribution and publication date verification.
Financial AI system cross-checks market data against official SEC filings, not just news headlines.
articles.build: Consultants are charging $5K-$15K to audit existing AI systems and retrofit them with source-aware verification, primarily for legal tech and compliance firms. Agencies building chatbots for healthcare and finance are offering this as a $500-$2K/month add-on to enterprise contracts. Some developers are selling pre-built MCP verification modules on GitHub Marketplace and Hugging Face as paid extensions.

At Meta's massive scale, even tiny latency increases directly tank ad performance metrics and revenue. Rather than accepting the performance regression that came with necessary kernel updates, Meta built a custom scheduling policy using sched_ext to maintain their latency requirements while staying current on kernel security and features. The solution is open-source, meaning other companies running high-throughput ad systems or latency-sensitive services can adopt the same approach. This represents a shift from writing closed-source kernel modules to leveraging the upstream Linux ecosystem—sched_ext is integrated into the mainline kernel, making it a sustainable long-term solution. The specific benefit: Meta can now upgrade their Linux kernel without sacrificing the sub-millisecond latency guarantees their ads delivery system depends on. This is particularly important because ad serving is one of the most latency-sensitive workloads in production—delays directly impact click-through rates, impressions served, and ultimately advertiser ROI.

Monitor real-time kernel scheduling performance and dynamically adjust CPU allocation for competing ad serving workloads.
Run production ads infrastructure on cutting-edge Linux kernels without accepting latency regressions from scheduler changes.

articles.headline: Meta Hits 10-Year Python Sponsorship Milestone With PSF
articles.body: Meta has officially marked its 10th consecutive year as a sponsor of the Python Software Foundation (PSF), the nonprofit organization that governs and supports the open-source Python programming language. This extended commitment underscores how deeply Python is woven into Meta's engineering infrastructure — the company uses it across its entire stack, from infrastructure to machine learning to backend systems. Python has become one of the world's most influential programming languages, powering everything from AI model development to data science to web backends, making it essential for any company at Meta's scale. By maintaining consistent sponsorship over a decade, Meta is investing in the ecosystem that underpins not just its own operations but the broader AI and software engineering industry. The PSF relies on corporate sponsors to fund development, community programs, conferences, and infrastructure that keep Python free and accessible to millions of developers globally. This type of long-term commitment signals Meta's belief that supporting foundational open-source tools creates competitive advantages and strengthens the talent pool available to the company.
examples: Use Python libraries like PyTorch to train large language models at scale.
Build internal infrastructure tools and automation scripts that power Meta's data centers.
Deploy Python-based AI services handling billions of requests daily across platforms.
articles.build: Python developers are monetizing this ecosystem shift by offering AI model training services, data pipeline consulting, and PyTorch optimization for startups — charging $150-500/hour for specialized Python engineering. Freelancers on Upwork and Toptal are seeing 30% higher rates for Python + ML expertise, with projects typically running 3-6 months and paying $40K-150K per engagement. Agencies are packaging Python-based AI infrastructure as a service, helping companies migrate legacy systems to modern Python stacks for $200K+ contracts.
